newsitem.title: UK: LME copper ends buoyant despite stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: LME copper ends buoyant despite stocks rise.

text.p: LME copper breached resistance on Tuesday, shrugging off a substantial inventory rise as the market was hit by renewed physical tightness in Europe.
"The nearby tightness has overshadowed the stocks situation," said analyst Robin Bahr of broker Brandeis.
Three month copper prices paused following the release of stocks data that showed a 11,475 tonne rise, but went on to steadily push up through resistance levels of $2,200 and $2,215.
The market ended the afternoon kerb at $2,221, up $26 and just $3 off its high. The premium of cash over three months metal firmed by about $15 to $120/$130.

The bulk of the stocks rise, a net 9,850 tonnes, was due to metal delivered into the Singapore warehouse, but inventories in Europe have been dwindling. Only 1,825 tonnes are now in Rotterdam after a rise on Tuesday of 1,125 tonnes.
"The problem with a lot of these metals is the geographical location...the brands needed by the market also may not be in the right location," Bahr said.
It was impossible to tell whether the stock rise was the start of a new trend or just a one-off.
"So many people have been wrong-footed by this market... people are still nervous," he added.
Resistance was pegged at $2,240/50, then the November 28 high of $2,313.

Nickel put in another good showing on Tuesday, galloping up by $220 to finish the kerb at $7,080, right in the middle of a resistance area based on previous highs of $7,090 and $7,070 on November 26 and 27 respectively.
The market lifted off on Monday on technical buying and short-covering after becoming oversold, erasing a whole month of losses in two days
Prices would now have to grind down a band of resistance between $7,170 and $7,250 to make further progress, Bahr said.
Aluminium finished the day $8.50 firmer at $1,560.50, ending near it highs but failing to confront important resistance at $1,570.
The market was rangebound and needed more time to consolidate before breaking higher, analysts say.
Tin closed the kerb $40 stronger at $5,800 and zinc ended $8 firmer at $1,072
Lead finishing barely changed at $695, down $1, while aluminium alloy finished stronger at $1,445 versus $1,430/35.
